Field Shelter in Nara / Studio Armitage

title: Eyes on the Street: Jane Jacobs’ Concept and Contemporary Residential Architecture in Brazil
text:
Eyes on the Street: Jane Jacobs’ Concept and Contemporary Residential Architecture in Brazil

The concept of "eyes on the street" is perhaps the most famous within architectural and urban literature when it comes to urban security. Jane Jacobs uses this expression to refer to people who - consciously or unconsciously - use public spaces or observe them from their homes, generating natural surveillance. A movement that, within our discipline, is encouraged both through quality public spaces and through the powerful relationship between the public and private created through building facades. Advocating for this daily control, Jacobs believes in a way of making architecture and cities that condemns excessive verticalization, reinforced by isolated buildings and single-use ones that deny contact with the street.

title: Family home Eemnes / Kumiki
text:
Family home Eemnes / Kumiki

On the edge of the Zuiderheide nature reserve in Eemnes stands a family home dating from 1971. The original house had a square footprint and measured just fifty square metres. An extension was added in 2002, but this resulted in a fragmented layout. The staircase was hidden away in a corner, the rooms were dark, and the spaces were poorly connected, both visually and in terms of circulation.

title: Colien House / Álvaro Siza Vieira
text:

title: Estúdio Semibreve / Estúdio Clara Nahas
text:
Estúdio Semibreve / Estúdio Clara Nahas

No Estúdio Semibreve, a materialização da narrativa exigiu um exercício rigoroso de zoneamento e uma subversão proposital da lógica habitacional. Em uma área de 55 metros quadrados, o Estúdio Clara Nahas estabelece uma planta de fluxo invertido, onde a hierarquia convencional entre o público e o privado é reordenada para priorizar o recolhimento. Diferente da recepção imediata por áreas sociais, a entrada acontece pela zona íntima. O visitante da mostra é convidado a percorrer o dormitório e o ambiente de estudo antes de alcançar a amplitude da convivência. Esta decisão projetual atua como um filtro sensorial: atravessar a intimidade torna-se um rito de passagem necessário para se conectar com a alma da casa, sugerindo que o despojamento pessoal deve preceder o encontro com o outro.

title: Basque Museum Bilbao / VAILLO + ARCHITECTS
text:
Basque Museum Bilbao / VAILLO + ARCHITECTS

The project is the outcome of a competition for the comprehensive architectural and museographic renovation and rehabilitation of the Euskal Museoa Bilbao—the Ethnographic Museum of Basque Culture. The complex of buildings that makes up the current museum is located on a city block in Bilbao's historic center; its origins date back to the 17th century with the founding of the first Society of Jesus (Jesuit) college in Bilbao in 1600.

title: Veja São Paulo Store / Roberto Somlo Arquitetura
text:
Veja São Paulo Store / Roberto Somlo Arquitetura

The project transforms an existing building on Oscar Freire Street, in the Jardim Paulista neighborhood, to house the first VEJA store in Brazil. The store is a radical encounter between exposed history and São Paulo modernism.

title: CitySquash / Gluck+
text:
CitySquash / Gluck+

CitySquash is a not-for-profit after-school enrichment program serving youth in the Bronx and Brooklyn through an integrated model of athletics, academics and mentorship. As the organization expanded beyond its existing scattered facilities serving more than 225 students annually, a new center was designed within the neighborhood it already serves, bringing these services together into a cohesive whole.

title: Success Academy Bronx K–12 Campus / SOM
text:
Success Academy Bronx K–12 Campus / SOM

Success Academy (SA)—one of the nation's largest and highest-performing public charter networks—educates 22,000 students, primarily from low-income backgrounds, across 60 New York City schools. Founded on the belief that all children can excel when given access to exceptional teaching and learning environments, SA is nationally recognized for its rigorous academics, robust arts and athletics programming, and deep focus on college preparedness. For its first ground-up building, the network charged SOM with creating a 310,000-square-foot K–12 "school of the future," with every aspect of the architecture supporting and reflecting SA's carefully crafted and boldly reinvented schooling practice.

title: Lele Hotel / The Lab Evn
text:
Lele Hotel / The Lab Evn

Located in Vayots Dzor, Lele Hotel is conceived as a direct response to the character and topography of its mountainous surroundings. Rather than imposing a separate architectural object on the landscape, the design seeks continuity with the terrain through its materiality, proportions, and relationship to the existing slope.

title: Buenos Aires Architecture City Guide: 31 Sites Between Heritage and the Contemporary
text:
Buenos Aires Architecture City Guide: 31 Sites Between Heritage and the Contemporary

Buenos Aires is a city of rich history and distinct atmospheres. There are many reasons to explore its architecture: the city is the result of a complex interplay of cultural factors shaped by a multitude of architectural styles and trends. Its streets and heterogeneous buildings define its inhabitants, reflecting an identity forged by its history.

title: Scaffolding as Interior Architecture: The Longevity of Temporary Structures
text:
Scaffolding as Interior Architecture: The Longevity of Temporary Structures

Scaffolding is perhaps one of architecture's most familiar temporary structures. It accompanies buildings through construction, maintenance, and renovation, only to disappear once its work is complete. Yet its apparent impermanence conceals a different kind of longevity. Scaffolding systems are designed to be assembled, dismantled, transported, and reused, with standardized components robust enough to withstand repeated handling and changing site conditions. Their temporary character lies less in the material itself than in the duration of each assembly.

title: Two Projects in Paris Win the European Collective Housing Award
text:
Two Projects in Paris Win the European Collective Housing Award

As cities struggle to provide adequate and affordable housing, examining built examples of collective housing can help inform decisions about what to build and how. These projects offer opportunities to assess solutions, understand their limitations, and consider what might be applied elsewhere. In Paris, two recent examples combine apartments of different sizes with access to gardens, courtyards, and other outdoor spaces, working with structures already in place.

title: CHYBÍK + KRIŠTOF Turns Aedes Into a Live Architecture Studio to Develop Four Berlin Projects
text:
CHYBÍK + KRIŠTOF Turns Aedes Into a Live Architecture Studio to Develop Four Berlin Projects

CHYBÍK + KRIŠTOF has opened Building the Existing City, an exhibition at Aedes Architecture Forum in Berlin that transforms the gallery into a working architecture studio. Running from October 23 to December 3, 2026, the exhibition centres on four architectural and urban design proposals for sites or urban situations in Berlin, selected through an open call. Over six weeks, visitors can follow the practice's research, discussions, and design work as the proposals develop, gaining insight into the processes through which architectural interventions are conceived in response to local conditions.

title: Tollymore House / McGonigle McGrath
text:
Tollymore House / McGonigle McGrath

Sited on the steep north bank of a 'spate' river in the shadow of the Mourne Mountains in County Down, this house takes its cue from the glacial river stones that line the river edge. It is a dwelling of six parts, embedded into the steep river bank, expressed as a collection of forms which are arranged so that each form lightly touches another.

title: Mecanoo Releases New Images of the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen Renovation in Rotterdam
text:
Mecanoo Releases New Images of the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen Renovation in Rotterdam

Delft-based practice Mecanoo has just released images of the renovation project for the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. The first images of the project were released in 2020, when the practice unveiled a proposal for a new wing as part of a larger renovation of the existing Museum Garden and a general reorganization of the layout to clarify circulation and connections throughout the complex. The comprehensive project includes a new building, the restoration and interior design of the existing premises, and a landscape project. The site, which has been closed since 2019 due to fire risk, water issues, overdue maintenance, and the presence of substantial amounts of asbestos, is a national monument expected to meet the updated standards and logistical requirements of an art institution of its kind.

title: Pavilions as Stances: 6 Unbuilt Proposals from the ArchDaily Community
text:
Pavilions as Stances: 6 Unbuilt Proposals from the ArchDaily Community

In architecture, the word "pavilion" can describe an endless variety of structures. It might be defined as a principle and a typology, a freestanding structure, a temporary intervention, a gathering place in the city, or a space for experimentation. This last quality is what unites the six unbuilt projects featured here, all designed and submitted by ArchDaily readers. Here, the definition lies in their sculptural qualities and formal exploration, while their permanence and location vary according to each structure's purpose. The proposals also demonstrate another quality inherent to the pavilion: the intention to symbolically represent a stance. Their exploration of form and material thus also reflects a search for a sense of boundary, wonder, or a shared future.

title: Ibiza House / Studio Metamorphosis
text:
Ibiza House / Studio Metamorphosis

There are places remembered for the way they are inhabited. Ibiza represents a way of living where time revolves around shade, landscape, and shared spaces. This was the starting point for Studio Metamorphosis when designing this vacation home in Albacete: to reinterpret the essence of traditional Ibizan (payesa) architecture without literally reproducing it, adapting it to a new context through a contemporary lens.

title: Blu Pizzeria Jeddah / movs studio
text:
Blu Pizzeria Jeddah / movs studio

Blu is a pizzeria chain where every restaurant takes its character from the city it opens in. For the Jeddah location, MOVS STUDIO built the interior around the element that shapes this Red Sea port: the wind. The restaurant occupies a corner unit of 335 square meters with a curved glazed facade. A terrace runs along the glass, and behind it the plan opens into one large hall, with the kitchen, storage, staff rooms and restrooms gathered in a compact service block at the rear.

title: Shenzhen Bay MixC Phase II / Ippolito Fleitz Group
text:
Shenzhen Bay MixC Phase II / Ippolito Fleitz Group

Where Infrastructure Becomes Experience - As retail environments continue to evolve globally, shopping malls are increasingly shifting from consumption-driven destinations into mixed-use social and cultural ecosystems. In this context, Shenzhen Bay MixC Phase II positions itself as an exemplary next-generation retail development—one that prioritises experience, connectivity, and urban integration over conventional commercial planning. As a major urban retail complex developed by China Resources Land in Shenzhen, the project redefines the role of the mall within the contemporary city. Rather than operating as a self-contained retail object, it becomes part of a larger urban network: a place where infrastructure, leisure, culture, and nature converge into a continuous spatial experience.

title: Mirador House / Rodrigo de la Cerda Arquitecto
text:
Mirador House / Rodrigo de la Cerda Arquitecto

A house that rotates to capture the view, shields itself from the wind, and adapts to the slope. Located in Mirador Punta Pite, Papudo, Chile, the house sits at elevation 240 on a steep hillside, in a privileged position facing the ocean, offering panoramic views of the landscape. Maximizing and enhancing this condition was one of the main objectives of the project.
